items.statement: Show that glove system materials for isolators and RABS have suitable mechanical and chemical resistance.
items.quote: The materials used for glove systems (for both isolators and RABS) should be demonstrated to have appropriate mechanical and chemical resistance.

items.statement: Define how often gloves are replaced in the contamination control strategy (CCS).
items.quote: The frequency of glove replacement should be defined within the CCS.

items.statement: Leak test isolator glove systems with a method shown to suit the task and its criticality.
items.quote: For isolators, leak testing of the glove system should be performed using a methodology demonstrated to be suitable for the task and criticality.

items.statement: Perform isolator glove system leak testing at defined intervals.
items.quote: The testing should be performed at defined intervals.

items.statement: As a general rule, test isolator glove integrity at least at the start and end of every batch or campaign.
items.quote: Generally glove integrity testing should be performed at a minimum frequency of the beginning and end of each batch or campaign.

items.statement: Carry out extra isolator glove integrity tests where the validated campaign length makes them necessary.
items.quote: Additional glove integrity testing may be necessary depending on the validated campaign length.

items.statement: Include in isolator glove integrity monitoring a visual check at every use and after any manipulation that could affect system integrity.
items.quote: Glove integrity monitoring should include a visual inspection associated with each use and following any manipulation that may affect the integrity of the system.

items.statement: For manual aseptic work producing single units or small batches, glove integrity verification frequency can be set on other criteria, e.g. start and end of each manufacturing session.
items.quote: For manual aseptic processing activities where single unit or small batch sizes are produced, the frequency of integrity verification may be based on other criteria, such as the beginning and end of each manufacturing session.
items.condition: manual aseptic processing of single units or small batches

items.statement: Perform integrity/leak testing of isolator systems at defined intervals.
items.quote: Integrity / leak testing of isolator systems should be performed at defined intervals.

items.statement: For RABS, sterilise grade A gloves before installation, and sterilise or effectively bio-decontaminate them by a validated method before every manufacturing campaign.
items.quote: For RABS, gloves used in the grade A area should be sterilised before installation and sterilised or effectively bio-decontaminated by a validated method prior to each manufacturing campaign.
items.condition: for RABS gloves in grade A

items.statement: For RABS, disinfect gloves by an approved method after each exposure to the background environment during operation.
items.quote: If exposed to the background environment during operation, disinfection using an approved methodology following each exposure should be completed.
items.condition: if RABS gloves exposed to background environment during operation

items.statement: For RABS, examine gloves visually at each use.
items.quote: Gloves should be visually examined with each use

items.statement: For RABS, integrity test gloves at periodic intervals.
items.quote: integrity testing should be performed at periodic intervals.

items.statement: Define and control decontamination methods for RABS/isolators (cleaning, bio-decontamination and, where applicable, inactivation of biological materials).
items.quote: Decontamination methods (cleaning and bio-decontamination, and where applicable inactivation for biological materials) should be appropriately defined and controlled.
items.condition: inactivation where applicable for biological materials

items.statement: Clean before the bio-decontamination step, since remaining residues may reduce decontamination effectiveness.
items.quote: The cleaning process prior to the bio-decontamination step is essential

items.statement: Have evidence that cleaning and bio-decontamination agents do not adversely affect product made in the RABS or isolator.
items.quote: Evidence should also be available to demonstrate that the cleaning and bio-decontamination agents used do not have adverse impact on the product produced within the RABS or isolator.

items.statement: For isolators, make interior bio-decontamination automated, validated and controlled within defined cycle parameters, using a sporicidal agent in a suitable form (e.g. gas or vapour).
items.quote: The bio-decontamination process of the interior should be automated, validated and controlled within defined cycle parameters and should include a sporicidal agent in a suitable form (e.g. gaseous or vaporized form).

items.statement: During isolator bio-decontamination, extend gloves with fingers separated so the agent contacts all glove surfaces.
items.quote: Gloves should be appropriately extended with fingers separated to ensure contact with the agent.

items.statement: Ensure isolator cleaning and sporicidal bio-decontamination leave interior surfaces and the critical zone free of viable microorganisms.
items.quote: Methods used (cleaning and sporicidal bio-decontamination) should render the interior surfaces and critical zone of the isolator free from viable microorganisms.

not_applicable.text: any residues that remain may inhibit the effectiveness of the decontamination process.

items.statement: For RABS, include in sporicidal disinfection the routine application of a sporicidal agent by a validated method shown to reach all interior surfaces and to give a suitable aseptic processing environment.
items.quote: The sporicidal disinfection should include the routine application of a sporicidal agent using a method that has been validated and demonstrated to robustly include all areas of the interior surfaces and ensure a suitable environment for aseptic processing.

items.statement: Qualify cleanrooms and clean air equipment (UDAF units, RABS, isolators) used for sterile manufacture against the environmental characteristics required.
items.quote: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment such as unidirectional airflow units (UDAFs), RABS and isolators, used for the manufacture of sterile products, should be qualified according to the required characteristics of the environment.
items.condition: used for manufacture of sterile products

items.statement: Provide each manufacturing operation with a suitable environmental cleanliness level in the operational state to minimise contamination risk to product or materials.
items.quote: Each manufacturing operation requires an appropriate environmental cleanliness level in the operational state in order to minimize the risk of contamination of the product or materials being handled.

items.statement: Maintain appropriate cleanliness levels in both the at rest and operational states.
items.quote: Appropriate cleanliness levels in the “at rest” and “operational” states should be maintained.

items.statement: Qualify cleanrooms and clean air equipment with a methodology that meets Annex 15.
items.quote: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment should be qualified using methodology in accordance with the requirements of Annex 15.

items.statement: Keep cleanroom qualification, including classification, clearly separate from operational environmental monitoring.
items.quote: Cleanroom qualification (including classification) should be clearly differentiated from operational environmental monitoring.

items.statement: Include installed filter system leakage and integrity testing in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: installed filter system leakage and integrity testing
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Include airflow volume and velocity tests in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: airflow tests - volume and velocity
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Include an air pressure difference test in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: air pressure difference test
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Include an airflow direction test with visualisation in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: airflow direction test and visualisation
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Include airborne and surface microbial contamination testing in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: microbial airborne and surface contamination
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Include a temperature measurement test in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: temperature measurement test
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Include a relative humidity test in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: relative humidity test
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Include a recovery test in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: recovery test
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Include a containment leak test in the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment, where relevant to the installation's design or operation.
items.quote: containment leak test
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Schedule and carry out cleanroom classification activities so they do not affect process or product quality.
items.quote: Classification activities should be scheduled and performed in order to avoid any impact on process or product quality.

items.statement: For cleanroom classification, measure total particles of 0.5 µm and larger and of 5 µm and larger.
items.quote: For cleanroom classification, the total of particles equal to or greater than 0.5 and 5 µm should be measured.

items.statement: Measure particles for classification both at rest and in simulated operations, against the Table 1 limits.
items.quote: This measurement should be performed both at rest and in simulated operations in accordance with the limits specified in Table 1.

items.statement: For classification, grade A must not exceed 3 520 particles/m3 of 0.5 µm or larger at rest or in operation; no limit is set for 5 µm or larger particles.
items.quote: Grade | Maximum limits for total particle ≥ 0.5 µm/m3 at rest | Maximum limits for total particle ≥ 0.5 µm/m3 in operation | Maximum limits for total particle ≥ 5 µm/m3 at rest | Maximum limits for total particle ≥ 5 µm/m3 in operation || A | 3 520 | 3 520 | Not specified^(a) | Not specified^(a)

items.condition: cleanroom classification at rest and in simulated operations

items.condition: cleanroom classification at rest and in simulated operations

items.quote: Classification including 5µm particles may be considered where indicated by the CCS or historical trends.
items.condition: where indicated by the CCS or historical trends

items.statement: For grade D, set in-operation particle limits based on risk assessment and, where applicable, routine data.
items.quote: The manufacturer should establish in operation limits based on a risk assessment and routine data where applicable.

items.statement: For classification of grade A and grade B areas, consider adding sample locations beyond the ISO 14644-1 minimum.
items.quote: For the aseptic processing area and the background environment (the grade A and grade B areas, respectively), additional sample locations should be considered
items.condition: classification of grade A and B areas

items.statement: Evaluate all critical processing areas, such as the point of fill and container closure feeder bowls, during classification of grade A and B areas.
items.quote: all critical processing areas such as the point of fill and container closure feeder bowls should be evaluated.
items.condition: classification of grade A and B areas

items.statement: Determine critical processing locations by documented risk assessment and knowledge of the process and operations in the area.
items.quote: Critical processing locations should be determined by documented risk assessment and knowledge of the process and operations to be performed in the area.

items.statement: Classify cleanrooms in both the at rest and in operation states.
items.quote: Cleanroom classification should be carried out in the “at rest” and “in operation” states.

items.statement: Achieve the Table 1 at-rest total particle limits after a clean-up period following completion of operations and line clearance/cleaning.
items.quote: The total particle limits given in Table 1 above for the “at rest” state should be achieved after a “clean up” period on completion of operations and line clearance/cleaning activities.
items.condition: after completion of operations and line clearance/cleaning

items.statement: Determine the clean-up period (guidance under 20 minutes) during room qualification, document it and follow it in procedures to restore qualified cleanliness if disrupted in operation.
items.quote: The "clean up" period (guidance value of less than 20 minutes) should be determined during the qualification of the rooms, documented and adhered to in procedures to reinstate a qualified state of cleanliness if disrupted during operation.

items.statement: Justify the unidirectional airflow air speed, including where it is measured, in the qualification protocol.
items.quote: The speed of air supplied by unidirectional airflow systems should be clearly justified in the qualification protocol including the location for air speed measurement.

items.statement: Design, measure and maintain air speed so unidirectional airflow protects product and open components at the working position (e.g. high-risk operations, exposed product/components).
items.quote: Air speed should be designed, measured and maintained to ensure that appropriate unidirectional air movement provides protection of the product and open components at the working position (e.g. where high-risk operations occur and where product and/or components are exposed).

items.statement: Unidirectional airflow systems should give a homogeneous air speed of 0.36–0.54 m/s (guidance value) at the working position, unless scientifically justified otherwise in the CCS.
items.quote: Unidirectional airflow systems should provide a homogeneous air speed in a range of 0.36 – 0.54 m/s (guidance value) at the working position, unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS.
items.condition: unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS

items.statement: Ensure airflow visualisation studies correlate with air speed measurements.
items.quote: Airflow visualization studies should correlate with the air speed measurement.

items.statement: Determine cleanroom microbial contamination levels as part of cleanroom qualification.
items.quote: The microbial contamination level of the cleanrooms should be determined as part of the cleanroom qualification.

items.statement: Base the number of microbial sampling locations for qualification on documented risk assessment, classification results, air visualisation studies and process knowledge.
items.quote: The number of sampling locations should be based on a documented risk assessment and the results obtained from room classification, air visualization studies and knowledge of the process and operations to be performed in the area.

items.statement: Cover both at rest and in operation states in microbial qualification of cleanrooms.
items.quote: Qualification should include both “at rest” and “in operation” states.

items.statement: During qualification, grade A must show no growth for air samples, settle plates (90 mm, per 4 hours) and contact plates (55 mm).
items.quote: Grade | Air sample CFU/m3 | Settle plates (diameter 90 mm) CFU/4 hours^(a) | Contact plates (diameter 55 mm) CFU/plate || A | No growth

items.statement: During qualification, grade B limits are 10 CFU/m3 air, 5 CFU per 90 mm settle plate per 4 hours and 5 CFU per 55 mm contact plate.
items.quote: Grade | Air sample CFU/m3 | Settle plates (diameter 90 mm) CFU/4 hours^(a) | Contact plates (diameter 55 mm) CFU/plate || B | 10 | 5 | 5

items.quote: Grade | Air sample CFU/m3 | Settle plates (diameter 90 mm) CFU/4 hours^(a) | Contact plates (diameter 55 mm) CFU/plate || C | 100 | 50 | 25

items.statement: Expose settle plates for the duration of operations, changing them as required after at most 4 hours.
items.quote: Settle plates should be exposed for the duration of operations and changed as required after a maximum of 4 hours.

items.statement: Base settle plate exposure time on recovery studies and do not let the media dry out.
items.quote: Exposure time should be based on recovery studies and should not allow desiccation of the media used.

items.statement: Use every method listed for a grade in Table 2 when qualifying an area of that grade.
items.quote: All methods indicated for a specific grade in the table should be used for qualifying the area of that specific grade.

items.statement: Justify the approach if a tabulated method is omitted or alternative methods are used for qualification.
items.quote: If one of the methods tabulated is not used, or alternative methods are used, the approach taken should be appropriately justified.
items.condition: if a tabulated method is not used or alternative methods are used

items.statement: Where technologies reporting results other than as CFU are used, scientifically justify the applied limits and, where possible, correlate them to CFU.
items.quote: If different or new technologies are used that present results in a manner different from CFU, the manufacturer should scientifically justify the limits applied and where possible correlate them to CFU.
items.condition: if technologies report results other than in CFU

items.statement: Apply the Table 6 contact plate and glove print limits when qualifying personnel gowning.
items.quote: For the qualification of personnel gowning, the limits given for contact plates and glove prints in Table 6 should apply.

items.statement: Ensure sampling methods do not create a contamination risk to manufacturing operations.
items.quote: Sampling methods should not pose a risk of contamination to the manufacturing operations.

The maximum limits for microbial contamination during qualification for each grade are given in Table 2.
Limits are applied using CFU throughout the document.

items.statement: Requalify cleanrooms and clean air equipment periodically according to defined procedures.
items.quote: The requalification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment should be carried out periodically following defined procedures.

items.statement: Include, as a minimum, cleanroom classification (total particle concentration) in cleanroom and clean air equipment requalification.
items.quote: cleanroom classification (total particle concentration)

items.statement: Include, as a minimum, integrity testing of final filters in cleanroom and clean air equipment requalification.
items.quote: integrity test of final filters

items.statement: Include, as a minimum, airflow volume measurement in cleanroom and clean air equipment requalification.
items.quote: airflow volume measurement

items.statement: Include, as a minimum, verification of air pressure differences between rooms in cleanroom and clean air equipment requalification.
items.quote: verification of air pressure difference between rooms

items.statement: Include, as a minimum, an air velocity test in cleanroom and clean air equipment requalification.
items.quote: air velocity test

items.statement: For grades B, C and D, perform the air velocity test according to a risk assessment documented in the CCS.
items.quote: For grade B, C and D the air velocity test should be performed according to a risk assessment documented as part of the CCS.
items.condition: for grades B, C and D

items.statement: Perform the air velocity test for filling zones supplied with unidirectional airflow (e.g. filling terminally sterilised products, or background to grade A and RABS).
items.quote: However, it is required for filling zones supplied with unidirectional airflow (e.g. when filling terminally sterilised products or background to grade A and RABS).
items.condition: filling zones supplied with unidirectional airflow

items.statement: For grades with non-unidirectional airflow, replace velocity testing with a recovery test measurement.
items.quote: For grades with non- unidirectional airflow, a measurement of recovery testing should replace velocity testing

items.statement: Requalify grade A and B areas at intervals of no more than 6 months.
items.quote: The maximum time interval for requalification of grade A & B areas, is 6 months.

items.statement: Requalify grade C and D areas at intervals of no more than 12 months.
items.quote: The maximum time interval for requalification of grade C & D areas, is 12 months.

items.statement: Carry out appropriate requalification, including at least the listed tests, after remedial action for an out-of-compliance equipment or facility condition, or after changes to equipment, facility or processes as appropriate.
items.quote: Appropriate requalification consisting of at least the above tests should also be carried out following completion of remedial action implemented to rectify an out of compliance equipment or facility condition or after changes to equipment, facility or processes as appropriate.
items.condition: after remedial action or changes to equipment, facility or processes

items.statement: Determine the significance of a change (for requalification) through the change management process.
items.quote: The significance of a change should be determined through the change management process.

items.statement: Clean and disinfect cleanrooms thoroughly according to a written programme.
items.quote: They should be cleaned and disinfected thoroughly in accordance with a written programme.

items.statement: Clean surfaces to remove contamination before disinfecting them.
items.quote: For disinfection to be effective, prior cleaning to remove surface contamination should be performed.

items.statement: Ensure cleaning programmes effectively remove disinfectant residues.
items.quote: Cleaning programmes should effectively remove disinfectant residues.

items.statement: Use more than one type of disinfectant so that, where modes of action differ, their combined use is effective against bacteria and fungi.
items.quote: More than one type of disinfecting agent should be employed to ensure that where they have different modes of action, their combined usage is effective against bacteria and fungi.

items.statement: Include periodic use of a sporicidal agent in cleanroom disinfection.
items.quote: Disinfection should include the periodic use of a sporicidal agent.

items.statement: Monitor regularly to assess disinfection programme effectiveness and detect changes in microbial flora types (e.g. organisms resistant to the current regime).
items.quote: Monitoring should be undertaken regularly in order to assess the effectiveness of the disinfection programme and to detect changes in types of microbial flora (e.g. organisms resistant to the disinfection regime currently in use).

items.statement: Validate the cleanroom disinfection process.
items.quote: The disinfection process should be validated.

items.statement: Show in validation studies that disinfectants are suitable and effective as actually used and on the surface material (or justified representative material), and support in-use expiry periods of prepared solutions.
items.quote: Validation studies should demonstrate the suitability and effectiveness of disinfectants in the specific manner in which they are used and on the type of surface material, or representative material if justified, and should support the in-use expiry periods of prepared solutions.
